correctness.rationale: The commuting norm-convergent involution product gives an exact independent-bit transition law on finite subsets; summability bounds infinitely many flips. Viete duplication yields the exact singleton probability and resonant tail. A globally valid rescaled formula bounds y outside (0,2) and away from \(\pi/2\), forcing all maximizing times into the unique resonance window. A sinc bound forces local deviations delta to 0; strict logarithmic concavity and analytic implicit differentiation establish the unique sufficiently-high-index maximum and the stated \(2^{-m}\) and \(4^{-m}\) corrections. Exact first principles and 142 finite independent Fourier/product/numerical checks agree. Finite calculations do not prove the global statement.

value.rationale: State-to-singleton transfer probability optimized over all observation times is a natural operational invariant of a quantum walk. The explicit geometric weight already singled out in the source furnishes a nontrivial transition between finite perfect transfer and an infinite system with a sharp nonperfect \(4/\pi^2\) ceiling. The self-similar probability packet, exact fidelity, unique asymptotically optimized time, and first finite-index correction quantify both achievable remote excitation and unavoidable leakage. They are not a mere renaming of the known spectral interval or a fixed-time numerical table.
